1.n: = ἔφατο (τ → θ before rough breathing): Odysseus, at the end of his tale (12.453)

2.n: 'enchantment' (κηλέω 'charm'), the spell of his story; in Homer only here and 11.334
aorist middle with passive force, 'were held fast'
of large rooms lit only through narrow openings

3.n: unaugmented (= ἐφώνησε); second accent from enclitic τε

4.n: contracted -ευ (= ἵκεο, Attic ἵκου), this form only here in Homer; with ποτί + acc. of the goal
'with floor of bronze'; ποτὶ χαλκοβατὲς δῶ as 8.321, Iliad 1.426

5.n: 'therefore' (old dative of ὁ), opening the main clause after ἐπεί (4); Monro finds enough evidence in Homer for an adverbial τῶ distinct from the dative τῷ (Monro on 13.5)

5.p: verb · aor. part. pass. acc. sg. masc.

7.n: epic gen. ὑμέων = ὑμῶν; partitive with ἀνδρὶ ἑκάστῳ

7.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
7.n: middle 'enjoin, lay a charge on', + dat.: 'I say this as a charge'

8.n: epic -σσ-; antecedent ὑμέων (7), hence the second-person verbs πίνετʼ, ἀκουάζεσθε (9)
the honor-wine of the elders (γέροντες), the council of chiefs, as Iliad 4.259

9.n: + gen.; 'please yourselves with listening' (Monro on 13.9, comparing Iliad 4.343): verbs of this formation are ampliative, and often unfavorable in sense; in Homer again only 9.7 and Iliad 4.343

10.n: μὲν δή: the clothes are there already
dative of interest; Ionic ξεῖνος = ξένος
'chest, coffer', feminine: the chest Arete brought out at 8.438

11.n: singular verb with the neuter plural εἵματα (10) and χρυσός

12.n: 'counsel-bearing', used as a noun: the twelve kings of 8.390, who brought gifts
epic aorist ἔνεικα of φέρω (= ἤνεγκαν)

13.n: used as an interjection; ἀλλʼ ἄγε οἱ δῶμεν as 8.389
Eustathius read ἠέ 'or', though he found ἠδέ in the better manuscripts (Monro's critical note on 13.13)

14.n: 'man by man', each of us (ἀνήρ); only here in Homer

14.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
14.n: middle 'collect for ourselves', a levy to make good the gifts

15.n: ἐστί understood; its subject is χαρίσασθαι

'as a free gift', without repayment: originally a partitive genitive, 'of his bounty', used as an adverb like Attic προῖκα; Monro thinks the Homeric form probably πρόϊξ, a compound of πρός (Monro on 13.15); in Homer only here and 17.413

16.n: epic ἐπιανδάνω = ἐφανδάνω (ἐπιανδάνει Iliad 7.407): ἐπι- unelided before the lost ϝ- of ἁνδάνω 'please'; + dat.; the half-line again 16.406, 18.50 and later

17.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
17.n: apocope κακ- (= κατα-); desiderative: 'to go to bed'
οἶκον with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word
singular in apposition to the plural subject

18.n: the line = 2.1, 10.187, 12.8, Iliad 1.477 and often; the morning of the 34th day of the action (Monro on 13.18)

19.n: νῆα (νηῦς 'ship') with the suffix -δε 'to', elided, printed as one word; only here in Homer; the reading of Aristarchus and the Etymologicum Magnum, the vulgate νῆʼ ἄρʼ (Monro's critical note on 13.19)

the gifts of bronze, the tripods and cauldrons of 13

20.n: = κατέθηκε (κ → χ before the rough breathing of ἱερόν); with ὑπὸ ζυγά (21) (Monro on 13.21)

25.n: dative of Ζεύς (stem Ζην-); the line = 9.552

59.n: a parting wish, 'fare well'; second accent from enclitic μοι

65.n: epic acc. (Attic ναῦν); ἐπὶ νῆα θοὴν καὶ θῖνα θαλάσσης as 10.154, 10.407

70.n: the line = 2.407, 8.50 (4.428, 12.391 in the first person)

77.n: dative of manner: each in his place

79.n: dative of the person with ἐπὶ βλεφάροισιν: 'upon his eyelids'

imperfect: sleep came over him as they rowed

80.n: 'from which one does not wake' (νη- + ἐγείρω); in Homer only here and 74

80.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

87.g: could have kept pace with her

91.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

irregular superlative, related to φαεινός and φάος; only here in Homer

96.n: the old god of the sea, as 1.72; his harbor again 345

epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative with καταιβαταί
